metadata.note: The D&H's Lake George Branch - the resort line that carried summer traffic from the New York-Montreal main line at Fort Edward up to the foot of Lake George, where the trains met the lake steamboats. The Glens Falls Rail Road Company was incorporated July 26, 1867 and opened from Fort Edward to Glens Falls in 1869, being leased to the Rensselaer & Saratoga under a lease dated June 24, 1869. Thirteen years later it was pushed the rest of the way: the Caldwell extension from Glens Falls to Lake George village was completed May 29, 1882, and a new lease dated January 9, 1882 covering the extended property passed it to the Presidents, Managers & Company of the Delaware & Hudson Canal Company. The Glens Falls Rail Road was merged into the Rensselaer & Saratoga on July 31, 1906; at its demise it was a single-track standard-gauge railroad running the roughly 14.46 miles from Fort Edward to Lake George. The last scheduled passenger train arrived at Lake George station in November 1957, and freight was discontinued less than six months later. Station order: Lake George (Caldwell) - Glen Lake - Glens Falls - Fort Edward.

geometry_sources: Wikimedia Commons map data behind the Delaware and Hudson Railway article's system map (Data:Rensselaer and Saratoga Railroad.map, CC-BY-4.0), which is OSM-derived. The branch is split across two features there and is carried here the same way: 'Glens Falls Rail Road' (Fort Edward-Glens Falls, 9.0 km) and 'Rensselaer and Saratoga Rail Road (Lake George Extension)' (Glens Falls-Lake George, 15.6 km).

Independently cross-checked against OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API), where the same alignment is tagged across 25 ways under a spread of names - 'former D&H Lake George Branch', 'Warren County Bikeway (former D&H Lake George Branch)', 'CP Rail (former D&H Glens Falls/ Lake George Branch', 'D&H Lake George Branch'. The Commons geometry agrees with the OSM ways to a median of 0.4 m (p90 0.6 m), so the two are effectively the same survey.

The two features meet in Glens Falls with a 337 m gap between the Commons polylines (43.3127,-73.6343 to 43.3121,-73.6384) which is left as-is rather than bridged, so the branch renders as two touching segments. Combined traced length is 24.85 km / 15.44 miles against the ICC's documented 14.46 miles; the excess is most likely terminal and yard trackage included at the ends of the Commons trace.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact timetables and frequencies for any era; every headway below is estimated and unsourced. The November 1957 end date is sourced specifically for trains arriving at LAKE GEORGE - the end of passenger service on the Fort Edward-Glens Falls section is not separately sourced and is assumed here to be the same. The Hudson Valley Railway electric interurban, which also ran between Glens Falls and Lake George and is present in OSM as 'Hudson valley Rwy', is a different company and is not traced here. The D&H's South Glens Falls Branch and the Prospect Mountain Railway (a cable incline at Lake George) are likewise not included.

Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

A new lease dated January 9, 1882 passed the extended property to the Delaware & Hudson Canal Company. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
